newsitem.title: CHINA: China to salvage warships sunk by Japan in 1894.
newsitem.headline: China to salvage warships sunk by Japan in 1894.

text.p: A northeastern Chinese city plans to soon salvage four Qing dynasty warships sunk by the Japanese navy more than 100 years ago, the Ningxia Daily said in an edition seen in Beijing on Monday.
Donggang city in Liaoning province planned to retreive the vessels from the depths of the Yellow Sea and to build a memorial hall to the disastrous 1894-1895 Sino-Japanese war, the newspaper said.

Japan's overwhelming victory in the war, ended only by Beijing's acceptance of a humiliating "unequal treaty", was a critical blow for the Qing dynasty of imperial rulers and helped speed its collapse in 1911.
China is currently embroiled in a disagreement with Japan over the ownership of group of islands in the East China Sea that have been claimed by Japan since the 1895 treaty.

The Donggang city government would cooperate with a number of state historical organisations in salvaging the four warships, the newspaper said in a story headlined: "Revive history as a warning to posterity".
It gave no details of how the vessels would be salvaged or when the attempt would begin.
